_comment: MODEL-OS LEDGER — the single machine-readable source of truth for model routing across ALL repos and BOTH CLIs (Claude Code + Codex). Doctrine lives in model-os/MODEL-OS.md and reasons in ROLES; model NAMES live only here. Edit THIS file when the landscape shifts (new model, limit change, capability re-rank) — nothing else changes. Read by hooks/model-os-health.mjs (SessionStart), hooks/model-os-gate.mjs (PreToolUse Agent), and the Codex AGENTS block. last_verified + stale_after_days drive the staleness flag: a stale ledger is surfaced BEFORE heavy work, never silently trusted.
verification_log: 2026-07-09: corrected against live evidence, not priors. (1) Fable 5 confirmed GA (this session ran on it end-to-end; Anthropic's claude-api skill lists it in the current pricing/model table as 'most intelligent generally available model... sits above Opus in capability') — flipped from a 'verify-availability' placeholder to taste-canon PRIMARY. (2) codex model id corrected from the invented 'gpt-5.5-codex' to the real string 'gpt-5.5' — confirmed directly from ~/.codex/config.toml (model = "gpt-5.5") and a live `codex exec` probe echoing 'model: gpt-5.5'; local default effort is 'xhigh'. (3) Added sourced strengths/weaknesses for Opus 4.8 vs GPT-5.5 from WebSearch (DataCamp, CodingFleet, MindStudio/DeepSuite comparisons, July 2026): Opus 4.8 leads SWE-bench Pro (69.2% vs 58.6%) and multi-file/root-cause debugging; GPT-5.5 leads Terminal-Bench 2.0 (82.7% vs 74.6%) and near-ties SWE-bench Verified (88.7% vs 88.6%) — i.e. GPT-5.5's edge is agentic/terminal execution, which is exactly the independent-review lane's job (verifying rendered/executed artifacts), not a case for making it a build-primary.

2026-07-09 (audit implementation): full-framework audit findings implemented, founder-ratified. (1) Workflow-bypass gate closed — the gate hook now also matches the Workflow tool and blocks scripts calling agent() with no model: routing anywhere (the one ungated fan-out path). (2) billing_watch mechanism added (generic, dated) — first use: Fable 5's 2026-07-12 move to metered credits; the health hook flags it 7 days out and loudly once active, so the no-surprise-bills guarantee doesn't depend on memory. (3) acknowledged_candidates added — reviewed-not-adopted ids stop re-proposing every cycle (anti alert-fatigue); the weekly workflow now updates one standing issue instead of opening a new one per run. (4) FALLBACK-LOG.md created + doctrine wired — the 'wanted X, fell to Y' evidence the refresh loop greps now has a real file that sessions append to. (5) Health hook now prints the per-repo synced-copy age and flags >30d staleness. Billing audit verdict recorded: recurring metered spend ≈ $0 (workflow hits free list endpoints only; all interactive work on subscriptions); idea-lab's dormant agentic crons (daily-run/weekly-run.yml) confirmed keyless and no-op — do NOT set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as an idea-lab repo secret without meaning to activate them.

2026-07-09 (later): two founder-flagged current events, checked via WebSearch rather than taken on faith. (1) Fable 5's GA status has a real backstory the earlier entry missed: shipped 2026-06-09, pulled offline 2026-06-12 by a US export-control order, redeployed 2026-07-01 after Commerce lifted it (Anthropic's own 'Redeploying Fable 5' post) with a new safety classifier. Current 'status: current' / taste-canon-primary stands — but a real, DATED change is coming: after 2026-07-12, Fable 5 stops counting toward weekly plan limits and moves to metered usage credits instead (was: included in the $200/mo Max weekly cap). The anthropic-max budget lane's 'plan' description below is now stale for Fable specifically as of that date — see its updated note. (2) OpenAI publicly launched GPT-5.6 (three variants: Sol/Terra/Luna; Terra pitched as GPT-5.5-parity at half the cost) TODAY per CNBC/Neowin — but checked directly against the live Models API (same key/method refresh-research.mjs uses) and it does NOT appear yet (120 ids returned, same as the earlier same-day check; no id containing '5.6'/'sol'/'terra'/'luna'). NOT added to the ledger — unverifiable-live is not a basis for a model entry, no matter how well-sourced the announcement. This is exactly what the refresh mechanism is for: re-run `node model-os/refresh-research.mjs` (or wait for Monday's scheduled run) once it's actually queryable, and it will surface as a normal new-candidate proposal, no advance/hardcoded knowledge required. Also shipped this session: a relevance filter in refresh-research.mjs (family+recency gates, both self-relative to the ledger's own entries) that cut a 79-line noisy proposal list down to 14 genuinely-relevant candidates — see the script's own header comment for the design.

independent-review.job: Cross-provider review — ALWAYS the other provider from the author. From Claude-authored work: codex (gpt-5.5). From Codex-authored work: claude (fable/opus for taste surfaces, sonnet for code).
independent-review.notes: No same-provider substitute exists for this role by definition; lane down => 'review: pending', recorded. gpt-5.5 is well-suited here independent of the review-direction rule: Terminal-Bench leader (agentic/execution verification) even though it trails Opus 4.8 on raw multi-file build quality — reviewing rendered/executed output is exactly its strength.

caps.fanout_width_note: A wider fan-out is fine when the task genuinely needs it — state the width + why in the plan BEFORE launching (LES-105: 2 research agents self-expanded to 5 and burned ~450k tokens on a single-job product).
caps.subagent_respawn: Subagents do NOT spawn their own subagents unless the orchestrator's plan names it explicitly.
caps.top_tier_calibre_line: Any subagent launch on a requires_calibre_line model must carry 'calibre: <role> — <one-line why>' in its prompt; the gate hook blocks it otherwise.
caps.scheduled_runs_note: Scheduled/recurring tasks are the biggest silent burner and can't pin a model — keep the app default on the fan-out tier and route heavy work DOWN from the prompt, never up.

acknowledged_candidates._comment: Ids the refresh loop surfaced and the founder reviewed WITHOUT adopting — they stop re-appearing as proposals every cycle (alert fatigue is how a loud mechanism decays into a silent one). Acknowledging is 'seen, declined for now', never 'never': remove an id from this list to re-surface it. Genuinely NEW ids (e.g. a future gpt-5.6 family) are unaffected and always surface.

providers_extension: To add a provider (grok, gemini, ...): add a budget lane + model entries with strengths/weaknesses/access, then slot the models into role ladders where they earn a place. Roles and doctrine never change; only this ledger does.
resolution_extension: Any model whose live id is readable from a LOCAL CLI config file carries a `resolution` block (see the codex entry): method 'local-config' · source (the CLI's name, display-only) · config_path ('$VAR/... (fallback: ~/..., %VAR%\...)' syntax — env tokens + ~ expanded, fallbacks tried in order by hooks/resolve-local-models.mjs) · field (the config key holding the model id) · optional effort_field · cached_at. `id`/`default_effort` remain the cached values everything routes against (the gate hook and role ladders read them statically); the SessionStart health hook re-resolves the live file every session and flags LEDGER DRIFT on mismatch — loudly, for a human to fix; it NEVER self-writes this file. A resolver that can't find the file/field fails soft (the CLI may not be installed here) — absence is not drift. To cover a second CLI-backed provider: add a resolution block to its entry, nothing else — the resolver is provider-agnostic and names no CLI.
